rights.title: Know Your Rights
rights.choosePrompt: Which right would you like to learn about?
rights.intro: Listen to short guidance, recognise warning signs, and choose a safe next step.
rights.area.label: Choose your province
rights.area.help: Choose Punjab or Sindh to see the applicable legal note.
rights.core.title: Essential rights
rights.core.body: The problems cotton workers report most often, plus the most serious risks.
rights.more.title: More protections
rights.legalNote: Coverage can depend on the province and work arrangement. Ask for case-specific help when needed.
rights.reporting.title: Report safely
rights.reporting.body: In this app you can report anonymously, confidentially, or with your name. A later legal process may have different privacy rules.
rights.facts.title: Important things to know
rights.source.sindhChild: Sindh Prohibition of Employment of Children Act 2017
rights.source.iloVoice: ILO account from women cotton workers
rights.source.pesticideStudy: Study of women cotton pickers in Sindh
rights.wages.title: Pay, deductions and wages
rights.wages.body: You should receive full, timely and fairly calculated pay without unexplained deductions.
rights.wages.guidance.1: Ask how the daily or piece rate, cotton weight and any deductions will be calculated.
rights.wages.guidance.2: A very low verbal agreement may not remove minimum-wage or equal-pay protection where it applies.
rights.wages.warning.1: Payment is delayed, partly withheld, paid below the agreed wage, or routed through someone who keeps a share.
rights.wages.warning.2: The recorded cotton weight changes, overtime is unpaid, or deductions are not explained.
rights.wages.action.1: Remember or record the work date, agreed wage, weight, amount received and who arranged the work.
rights.wages.action.2: Report non-payment, delayed payment, unequal pay or an unexplained deduction. Proof is helpful but optional.
rights.wages.province.Punjab: Agricultural pay must consider working hours and notified minimum-wage rates. Part II protections also apply through contractors and family arrangements.
rights.wages.province.Sindh: Women agricultural workers have rights to equal pay for the same work and no less than the notified minimum wage. Coverage for other arrangements should be checked.
rights.wages.story.intro: Full and timely pay matters. Check the agreed wage, the weight and every deduction.
rights.wages.story.agree.title: Make the wage clear
rights.wages.story.agree.body: Confirm the daily or per-weight wage and how cotton will be weighed.
rights.wages.story.compare.title: Check the calculation
rights.wages.story.compare.body: Compare the work, weight, deductions and money received.
rights.wages.story.report.title: Report missing pay
rights.wages.story.report.body: Use voice to report unpaid, delayed or unfairly reduced wages.
rights.wages.story.proof: An agreed low amount does not always replace minimum-wage or equal-pay protection.
rights.wages.facts.title: Three things your wage must make clear
rights.wages.fact.full: Receive your full wage at the agreed time.
rights.wages.fact.weight: See the cotton weight and the wage applied.
rights.wages.fact.deductions: Every deduction should have a clear reason.
rights.wages.action.remember: Remember the work date, agreed wage, weight and amount you received.
rights.wages.reportCta: Report a wage problem by voice
rights.pesticide.title: Sprays and chemical exposure
rights.pesticide.body: Sprayers and pickers can be harmed by fresh spray, residues, drift and unsafe containers.
rights.pesticide.story.1.title: Wait for the warning
rights.pesticide.story.1.body: Do not enter a freshly sprayed field.
rights.pesticide.story.2.title: Move away and wash
rights.pesticide.story.2.body: Rinse exposed skin and eyes with clean water.
rights.pesticide.story.3.title: Get urgent help
rights.pesticide.story.3.body: Breathing trouble or collapse needs urgent care.
rights.pesticide.guidance.1: Workers need warning about spraying, safe re-entry, suitable protection, washing water and clear handling instructions.
rights.pesticide.guidance.2: Children must be kept away from pesticides, spray equipment and chemical containers.
rights.pesticide.warning.1: Burning eyes, itching skin, headache, nausea, dizziness, breathing trouble or unusual weakness after field work.
rights.pesticide.warning.2: No warning before spraying, entry into a recently sprayed field, no washing water, or reused chemical bottles.
rights.pesticide.action.1: Move away from exposure, remove contaminated clothing and rinse skin or eyes with clean water.
rights.pesticide.action.2: Get urgent medical help for breathing trouble, collapse, confusion, repeated vomiting or severe eye exposure.
rights.pesticide.province.Punjab: Punjab's core safety duties apply to agricultural workers. Agrochemical handling and toxic exposure are prohibited hazardous work for people under 18.
rights.pesticide.province.Sindh: Pesticide exposure among women pickers is well documented. Children and adolescents must not perform prohibited hazardous chemical work.
rights.heat.title: Heat, hours and rest
rights.heat.body: Work should not continue in a way that creates serious heat danger or denies necessary rest.
rights.heat.story.1.title: Notice heat danger
rights.heat.story.1.body: Treat dizziness, weakness or confusion seriously.
rights.heat.story.2.title: Shade, water, rest
rights.heat.story.2.body: Stop work, cool down and drink safe water.
rights.heat.story.3.title: Report forced hours
rights.heat.story.3.body: Tell us about denied breaks or forced overtime.
rights.heat.guidance.1: Safe work needs drinking water, shade, recovery breaks and a pace that accounts for heat and physical effort.
rights.heat.guidance.2: Hours, overtime and rest protections depend on the province and employment arrangement.
rights.heat.warning.1: Fainting, confusion, hot dry skin, severe weakness or inability to drink can be a medical emergency.
rights.heat.warning.2: Forced overtime, no breaks, no shade, or pressure to continue despite illness or dangerous heat.
rights.heat.action.1: Stop work, move to shade, cool the body and drink safe water when heat symptoms begin.
rights.heat.action.2: Seek urgent help for confusion, collapse or worsening symptoms, and report denied breaks or forced hours.
rights.heat.province.Punjab: Agricultural remuneration must consider working hours. General hour limits may depend on whether the worker is legally treated as an employee.
rights.heat.province.Sindh: For women agricultural workers, the working day must not exceed eight hours and must remain within protected daylight limits.
rights.injury.title: Injury, tools and first aid
rights.injury.body: Unsafe tools, machinery, transport and untreated injuries are workplace safety concerns.
rights.injury.story.1.title: Stop unsafe work
rights.injury.story.1.body: Do not continue with a dangerous tool or machine.
rights.injury.story.2.title: Treat first
rights.injury.story.2.body: Safety and medical care come before evidence.
rights.injury.story.3.title: Report the hazard
rights.injury.story.3.body: Record the place and task only when it is safe.
rights.injury.guidance.1: Work equipment should be maintained and workers should receive suitable protection, information and first aid.
rights.injury.guidance.2: A worker should not be punished for raising a serious and immediate safety danger.
rights.injury.warning.1: Bleeding wounds, insect bites, electric hazards, unguarded machinery or unsafe transport.
rights.injury.warning.2: An injury is hidden, medical care is refused, or the worker is pressured to continue unsafe work.
rights.injury.action.1: Leave immediate danger and obtain first aid or medical care before collecting evidence.
rights.injury.action.2: Note the place, task and people present, then report the hazard or injury when safe.
rights.injury.province.Punjab: Core occupational-safety duties apply to agricultural workers and include risk management and protection from imminent danger.
rights.injury.province.Sindh: Unsafe cotton work is widely documented, but the exact legal route can depend on the worker's arrangement. Request case-specific support.
rights.equality.title: Harassment and equal treatment
rights.equality.body: Violence, sexual harassment, threats, retaliation and discriminatory treatment are not acceptable.
rights.equality.story.1.title: Recognise wrong behaviour
rights.equality.story.1.body: Threats, unwanted conduct and unequal treatment are not acceptable.
rights.equality.story.2.title: Move to safety
rights.equality.story.2.body: Stay near a trusted person when danger is immediate.
rights.equality.story.3.title: Report privately
rights.equality.story.3.body: Choose anonymous or confidential reporting when needed.
rights.equality.guidance.1: Protection covers physical, verbal and sexual conduct as well as intimidation and retaliation connected with work.
rights.equality.guidance.2: Equal treatment includes pay and opportunity without discrimination based on sex or other protected grounds.
rights.equality.warning.1: Unwanted touching, sexual demands, insults, threats, stalking, weapons or pressure to stay silent.
rights.equality.warning.2: Lower pay or worse treatment because of gender, community, religion, language, disability, age or migrant status.
rights.equality.action.1: Move to a safer place and contact a trusted person when there is immediate danger.
rights.equality.action.2: Choose anonymous or confidential app reporting when identification could increase risk.
rights.equality.province.Punjab: The Code prohibits discrimination, unequal remuneration, violence and harassment for workers, including agricultural workers under Part II.
rights.equality.province.Sindh: Women agricultural workers are protected from harassment, abuse and discrimination and have equal-pay rights.
rights.child.title: Child labour and education
rights.child.body: Work must not expose children to danger, forced labour or loss of education.
rights.child.story.1.title: Keep children from danger
rights.child.story.1.body: Keep them away from pesticides, heavy loads and unsafe tools.
rights.child.story.2.title: Protect education
rights.child.story.2.body: Work must not replace school, health or development.
rights.child.story.3.title: Protect their identity
rights.child.story.3.body: Report without naming the child when disclosure creates risk.
rights.child.guidance.1: Age rules differ by province, but hazardous work and the worst forms of child labour are prohibited.
rights.child.guidance.2: School attendance, health and development must not be displaced by work.
rights.child.warning.1: A child handles pesticides, heavy loads, dangerous tools, machinery or works long hours.
rights.child.warning.2: A child misses school, works under debt or threats, or becomes ill or injured from field work.
rights.child.action.1: Move the child away from immediate chemical, machinery or violence danger and seek medical help if needed.
rights.child.action.2: Report without naming the child when identity could increase risk.
rights.child.province.Punjab: Under 16 is treated as a child. Limited light work from 14 may be allowed for up to four hours a day without harming school; hazardous work is prohibited under 18.
rights.child.province.Sindh: Children under 14 cannot work in agricultural establishments. Ages 14 to 17 cannot perform prohibited hazardous work and have hour and education protections.
rights.forced.title: Forced or debt labour
rights.forced.body: No debt, advance, threat or custom should force a person to work or stop them from leaving.
rights.forced.story.1.title: Debt cannot trap you
rights.forced.story.1.body: An advance cannot justify threats or blocked movement.
rights.forced.story.2.title: Reach safety
rights.forced.story.2.body: Do not confront a threatening person alone.
rights.forced.story.3.title: Report restrictions
rights.forced.story.3.body: Tell us about debt, threats or withheld documents.
rights.forced.guidance.1: A wage advance is not permission to threaten a worker, restrict movement or create an endless debt.
rights.forced.guidance.2: Workers must be free from forced labour, bonded labour and compulsory work imposed through threats or penalties.
rights.forced.warning.1: The worker cannot leave, refuse overtime, change employer or return home because of debt or threats.
rights.forced.warning.2: Documents or wages are withheld, debt keeps increasing, armed threats are used, or family members inherit the debt.
rights.forced.action.1: Do not confront a threatening person alone. Move to safety and use a trusted phone or contact when possible.
rights.forced.action.2: Report the debt, advance, threat, restricted movement or withheld documents as forced-labour indicators.
rights.forced.province.Punjab: Forced and bonded labour are prohibited, bonded debt is extinguished, and agricultural workers receive these Part II protections.
rights.forced.province.Sindh: Bonded and forced labour are prohibited. The correct authority and protection route should be confirmed for the district.
rights.facilities.title: Water, shade and toilets
rights.facilities.body: Safe drinking water, shade, washing and dignified toilet access are basic parts of safe field work.
rights.facilities.story.1.title: Check the essentials
rights.facilities.story.1.body: Safe water, shade, washing and private toilets matter.
rights.facilities.story.2.title: Use clean water
rights.facilities.story.2.body: Never drink from pesticide or unsafe irrigation containers.
rights.facilities.story.3.title: Report what is missing
rights.facilities.story.3.body: Tell us what, where and how many workers are affected.
rights.facilities.guidance.1: Facilities must be usable in practice and should not expose women or other workers to harassment or loss of privacy.
rights.facilities.guidance.2: Washing water is especially important after dust, pesticide residue or chemical contact.
rights.facilities.warning.1: Workers avoid drinking because there is no toilet, or use unsafe water from chemical or irrigation containers.
rights.facilities.warning.2: No shade or washing point, locked toilets, unsafe women's facilities, or punishment for toilet breaks.
rights.facilities.action.1: Use safe water and leave dangerous heat or contamination when facilities are missing.
rights.facilities.action.2: Report which facility is missing, where it is needed and how many workers are affected.
rights.facilities.province.Punjab: Missing water, washing or sanitation can be reported as a workplace safety risk. Exact duties depend on the work arrangement.
rights.facilities.province.Sindh: Women agricultural workers have health and dignity protections. Missing safe facilities should be reported for case-specific action.
rights.contract.title: Contractors and written terms
rights.contract.body: The person arranging work should not hide the rate, deductions, debt or responsibility for payment.
rights.contract.story.1.title: Make terms clear first
rights.contract.story.1.body: Agree the task, rate, weight, date and deductions.
rights.contract.story.2.title: Keep a safe record
rights.contract.story.2.body: Keep a copy, receipt, message or trusted witness.
rights.contract.story.3.title: Report both parties
rights.contract.story.3.body: Name the contractor and the farm or landholder.
rights.contract.guidance.1: Clear terms should identify the work, rate, unit of measurement, payment time, deductions and any advance.
rights.contract.guidance.2: Using a labour contractor does not automatically remove the responsibility of the principal or landholder.
rights.contract.warning.1: The contractor changes the rate, adds fees, disappears with wages or refuses to explain deductions.
rights.contract.warning.2: A blank paper is signed, debt is not recorded, or the worker is told no one is responsible for payment.
rights.contract.action.1: Ask for written or recorded terms and keep any safe receipt, message or witness information.
rights.contract.action.2: Report both the contractor and the farm or person for whom the work was performed.
rights.contract.province.Punjab: Agricultural workers may demand a written agreement, including when engaged indirectly through contractors or family arrangements.
rights.contract.province.Sindh: Women agricultural workers may demand written terms and fair arbitration about pay, schedules, conditions and safety.
rights.maternity.title: Maternity and women workers
rights.maternity.body: Pregnancy, maternity and care needs must not be used to justify abuse or discriminatory treatment.
rights.maternity.story.1.title: Avoid fresh spray
rights.maternity.story.1.body: Pregnancy requires protection from hazardous exposure.
rights.maternity.story.2.title: Rest and seek care
rights.maternity.story.2.body: Ask for shade, water, safer duties and medical advice.
rights.maternity.story.3.title: Report discrimination
rights.maternity.story.3.body: Pregnancy must not cause threats, dismissal or lower pay.
rights.maternity.guidance.1: Women workers need protection from hazardous exposure, discrimination and retaliation related to pregnancy or maternity.
rights.maternity.guidance.2: Maternity leave and related benefits depend on the province and employment arrangement.
rights.maternity.warning.1: Pregnant workers are sent into recently sprayed fields or denied necessary rest and medical care.
rights.maternity.warning.2: A woman is dismissed, underpaid, threatened or denied work solely because of pregnancy or maternity.
rights.maternity.action.1: Avoid chemical exposure and obtain medical advice when pregnancy-related symptoms or exposure occur.
rights.maternity.action.2: Report discriminatory treatment and request province-specific maternity guidance.
rights.maternity.province.Punjab: The Code provides maternity protections for covered employees; agricultural coverage can depend on the legal work relationship.
rights.maternity.province.Sindh: Women agricultural workers have express maternity protection under the provincial Act.
rights.voice.title: Worker groups and collective voice
rights.voice.body: Workers can be safer and more effective when they raise shared problems together.
rights.voice.story.1.title: Identify the shared problem
rights.voice.story.1.body: Discuss wages, safety or facilities together.
rights.voice.story.2.title: Choose your representative
rights.voice.story.2.body: Workers should choose who speaks for the group.
rights.voice.story.3.title: Report retaliation
rights.voice.story.3.body: Protect contacts and seek recognised worker support.
rights.voice.guidance.1: Freedom of association includes forming or joining worker organisations and choosing representatives.
rights.voice.guidance.2: Collective action can address shared wages, safety, facilities, child labour and discrimination.
rights.voice.warning.1: A worker is threatened, dismissed or denied work for joining a group or raising a shared concern.
rights.voice.warning.2: The employer chooses the worker representative or prevents workers from meeting peacefully.
rights.voice.action.1: Keep group contact information private when disclosure may create retaliation risk.
rights.voice.action.2: Report retaliation and seek support from a recognised union or worker organisation.
rights.voice.province.Punjab: Agricultural workers have freedom-of-association protection, with procedures that may be further prescribed.
rights.voice.province.Sindh: Registered women agricultural workers may form associations or unions and pursue collective support.
rights.compensation.title: Medical care and compensation
rights.compensation.body: A work injury or occupational illness should be recorded and assessed for treatment and compensation.
rights.compensation.story.1.title: Explain the work link
rights.compensation.story.1.body: Tell medical staff when, where and during which task it happened.
rights.compensation.story.2.title: Keep medical records
rights.compensation.story.2.body: Safely keep papers, receipts and incident details.
rights.compensation.story.3.title: Request an assessment
rights.compensation.story.3.body: Report the case without assuming that payment is guaranteed.
rights.compensation.guidance.1: Pesticide illness, heat illness and injuries can be work-related even when symptoms appear later.
rights.compensation.guidance.2: Compensation and social-protection eligibility depend on worker status, registration and provincial law.
rights.compensation.warning.1: The employer hides an accident, refuses a record, pressures the worker to sign, or delays urgent care.
rights.compensation.warning.2: Medical costs and lost wages are left entirely with an injured worker without any assessment.
rights.compensation.action.1: Seek treatment first and tell the medical worker when and where the exposure or injury happened.
rights.compensation.action.2: Keep safe medical papers and report the injury for an eligibility assessment.
rights.compensation.province.Punjab: The Code contains workplace-compensation provisions, but entitlement depends on the facts and worker relationship.
rights.compensation.province.Sindh: Compensation and social-security coverage can vary for informal agricultural work. Request an individual assessment.
rights.migrant.title: Migrant and tenant workers
rights.migrant.body: Migrant status, residence, tenancy or sharecropping should not be used to justify threats or discrimination.
rights.migrant.story.1.title: Agree before work
rights.migrant.story.1.body: Clarify wages, housing, transport or crop share.
rights.migrant.story.2.title: Check shares and costs
rights.migrant.story.2.body: Keep documents and ask for a clear account.
rights.migrant.story.3.title: Report place and details
rights.migrant.story.3.body: Record the village, farm and safe arrangement details.
rights.migrant.guidance.1: Migrant workers need equal treatment, freedom of movement and safe access to wages and reporting.
rights.migrant.guidance.2: Tenant and sharecropper disputes may involve land or revenue law as well as labour rights.
rights.migrant.warning.1: Movement or documents are restricted, transport or housing is unsafe, or wages are withheld because the worker came from elsewhere.
rights.migrant.warning.2: Crop shares, input costs or debt are changed without a clear account, or eviction is threatened to force work.
rights.migrant.action.1: Record the village, farm, contractor and any safe details of the wage, debt or crop-share arrangement.
rights.migrant.action.2: Report discrimination or coercion and request referral for tenant or land issues when needed.
rights.migrant.province.Punjab: Agricultural rights extend across several paid, unpaid, family and contractor arrangements, but tenancy disputes may need separate legal help.
rights.migrant.province.Sindh: Women agricultural-worker protections include seasonal migrants and temporary residents; other tenancy questions may need specialist referral.

offline.error.networkUnavailable: The server cannot be reached. Check that the API is running and this phone is on the same network.
offline.error.serverIntakeUnavailable: This server does not accept complaints yet. The API needs to be updated on the host.
offline.error.validationFailed: Some saved report details are invalid. Please create the report again if retrying does not work.
offline.error.identityUnavailable: The protected identity is no longer available on this phone. Please create the report again.
offline.error.configurationInvalid: The app is not configured with a valid server address.
offline.error.mediaUnavailable: An attached file is no longer available on this phone.
offline.error.mediaPersistence: An attachment could not be saved securely on this phone. Select the attachment again and retry.
offline.error.uploadFailed: An attachment could not be uploaded.
offline.error.malwareDetected: An attachment was rejected by the security scan. Replace it or continue without it.
offline.error.mimeMismatch: An attachment's contents do not match its file type. Replace it or continue without it.
offline.error.unknown: The report could not be sent. Please try again.
offline.recovery.omitBody: The missing attachment will not be included. The rest of the report will be sent.
offline.recovery.omitAcceptedBody: Your complaint remains received. This attachment will be recorded as omitted.
offline.recovery.discardBody: This report and its saved attachments will be permanently removed from this phone.
offline.saved.title: Saved on this phone

offline.saved.missing: This saved report was not found.
persistence.schemaReset: Some local demo data was cleared after a storage update.

portal.sidebar.privacy: Sensitive worker information · Handle with care
portal.topbar.search: Search by case ID, issue or location
portal.dashboard.attentionNote: Prioritised by immediate risk, overdue response and worker follow-up.
portal.dashboard.patternsNote: Operational patterns, risk distribution and reporting quality in one view.
portal.dashboard.filtersNote: Use filters to review a region, issue type, priority or reporting period.
portal.dashboard.dateScopeNote: Dashboard figures update by complaint submission date. Use this to compare recent field activity without changing the case list.
portal.dashboard.firstActionNote: Average time from complaint receipt to first staff action.
portal.dashboard.resolutionTimeNote: Average time from receipt to resolved or closed outcome.
portal.dashboard.topIssueNote: Most frequent issue in the current filter selection.
portal.dashboard.riskNote: Understand whether pressure is coming from urgent risk or case-stage backlog.
portal.dashboard.accessNote: Use these patterns to spot where workers are reporting and which groups are visible in the channel.
portal.dashboard.qualityNote: Track privacy mode, worker outcomes and where AI-assisted cases still need human judgement.
portal.dashboard.humanReviewNote: Share of AI-assisted cases flagged for staff review.
portal.dashboard.lowConfidenceNote: AI failed or low-confidence share; higher values need careful human review.
portal.dashboard.reopenRateNote: Reopened cases as a share of resolved or closed cases.
portal.case.safety.immediateBody: Confirm worker safety and follow the emergency escalation procedure before routine case review.
portal.case.safety.currentBody: Review the reported risk and record a safeguarding action promptly.
portal.case.workerReportNote: Source information submitted by the worker. Treat this as the primary account.
portal.case.noStatement: No written or transcribed statement is available.
portal.case.workerViewNote: This preview excludes internal notes and shows the current mobile status message.
portal.case.aiAssistive: Assistive summary only. Verify against the original report.
portal.case.humanReviewBody: Check the suggestion before taking action.
portal.case.visibility.internalBody: This note remains in the staff case record.

portal.case.noActions: No lifecycle action is currently available.
portal.case.previewWorkerNote: Check worker-visible wording before saving a status or resolution update.

portal.analytics.section.accessNote: Higher volume can reflect improved trust and access, not poorer performance.
portal.analytics.section.aiNote: AI indicators measure review needs; they are not worker performance measures.
